title: The Distinction of Universals and the Meaning of the Head
english: The visionary one, possessing the mind of Christ and seeing God within, is not troubled. You are the praise of Israel; 'in you we shall be praised all day long' (Ps 145:1). Our fathers hoped in you (Ps 22:4). Our fathers, having hoped in you, were heard 'and were not put to shame' (Ps 22:5); for always receiving their prayers, you brought them to a state of favor, even if they should die through afflictions. For that which hears them when they cry out is not that which makes them be outside of the afflictions, but that which is outside of the harm brought by the afflictions; thus also it was interpreted: 'do not bring us into temptation' (Matt 6:13). Even if the holy ones praying seem not to be heard, all the more they are heard, because by remaining in afflictions they are proven as athletes. For what a failure it would be if one praying should turn away from the afflictions? Furthermore, 'our fathers' is in the presence of the Savior; you know that he counts himself in many ways according to the human manner. They hoped, and you saved them; they cried out to you and were saved. Not by leading them into nothingness, but by overcoming through afflictions. 'They cried out to you.' Having cried out, they were saved. And the cry we take to be the stretched-out prayer; for we do not cry out with a laughing voice, for thought is the word of the soul, and voice is the sound of the inner man.

They hoped in you and were not put to shame. I am a worm and not a man (Job 25:6). The fathers, having cried out to you, were not put to shame; for they have attained that of which they expected, that of which they hoped. Here he teaches blindness: 'I am a worm and not a man' (Job 25:6). The man does not deny being a man, but [he teaches] that the man is such, since he does not even perceptually call himself a worm. I am not therefore that man about whom it is said: 'for where there is strife and jealousy among you, are you not men?' (Jas 3:16); but I have the same disposition toward them, drawing everything for their sake. And this too can be understood: since his body did not come from the casting of a man's seed, but from the mere matter taken from the womb, according to this he calls himself a worm; for the worm does not come from a union, but from simple matter. And here, from the simple matter subject to the female, the body arose for him. 'In it' indeed 'has been born' and 'has been born from it.' But the other bodies are said to be 'through women' [by way of] the washing...

To receive. Since therefore this one did not have her birth from the seed of a man, it did not happen through her, but from her. A reproach of men and a disgrace of a people. I am a reproach not simply of men, but of the 'men'. All those who, looking at me, mocked me.

Some wish to falsely make the universal many times; for the universal is sometimes cut and becomes universal in another way. If I say, 'All men are mortal,' I say this universally. But if I say that 'all the grammarians,' I speak of certain men, and the universal has come from the grammarian, not from the man. 'All the diligent are righteous.' I do not say this that 'all men [are righteous].' So also here: not all those looking at him mocked him—for indeed the apostles, looking, did not mock him—but all those looking at him in this way as a disgrace of a people, as a reproach; for the others did not look at him in this way.

They spoke with lips, they moved the head. If they had spoken from the heart, they would not have moved the head. They spoke with lips to many. And it is not a wonder if they said these things concerning the one who suffered and was seen hanging. And God himself blames them, saying, 'This people honors me with their lips' (Ps 51:17). Therefore all the hypocrites, when they rejoice with the holy and the righteous, speak only with lips. And those who indeed boast grandly about the Savior were doing this: 'But [he said] the one destroying the temple and in three days building it up' (Mk 14:58).

Furthermore: to move the head? Perhaps even regarding history; they did this by cutting corners. And often the head signifies the mind. When anyone thus speaks against the Savior with lips without having seen him as he ought to be, he has a shaken mind, he has a wavering mind. Because the head signifies the mind: 'I have given their paths into [their] heads' (Ps 101:8), and this head did not possess anything of itself. 'And from thence he will come out, and your hands shall be upon your head; you will say, I have not sinned; for behold, I am judged against you' (Zech 10:5). And coming out of this life, you will have your deeds upon your head. And also: 'His pain shall return upon his head' (Job 34:31). But also praiseworthily: 'The eyes of the wise are in his head' (Prov 2:10). And he who, being not wise, has become wise, does not have [them] being carried around.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The progression from milk to spiritual strength
english: The eyes are moved to another place. Thus he says that the insight of the wise man is in his head according to Christ; for 'his head is the Christ' (Ps 22:1). He hoped in the Lord; let Him rescue him; let Him save him, because He wills him. Mockers say so. He said that men have also been accustomed to say such things concerning the righteous who are afflicted: 'If he is willed by Him, let Him save him'. And He will rescue him, not because they say this, but because he is willed by Him. He executes His own economy. He came to fulfill the will of the Father; for 'I have come down from heaven not to do my own will' (Jn 6:38). If therefore he does the will of his Father, He wills him.

For 'you are the one who burst me forth from the womb' (Ps 22:9). And regarding the history, something plausible might be said. Mary received 'the Holy Spirit coming upon her and the power of the Most High overshadowing her' (Lk 1:35). And just as God Himself forms bodies in the womb—as He formed Jeremiah and this body in the womb of Mary. Since therefore the same purity and cleanness were regarding the body, He Himself burst it forth from the womb. He did not do something great in this, but just as having formed Adam he showed him to be a man, so having formed him he brought him forth.

'My hope is from the breasts of my mother' (Ps 22:10). Even while still nursing you showed yourself, that you are my hope, having called the Magi—for while still an infant he mastered magic. In receiving milk I was not acting like an infant as other infants are ignorant of God, but I held hope in you.

'Upon you I was cast forth from the womb' (Ps 22:9). He, not having done sin nor having deceit in his heart, he who 'before knowing calls father and mother' (Ps 22:11) took 'the power of Damascus and the cunning of Samaria', he who 'before evil things came forth' chose 'the good'; for this shows that he neither did sin nor knew it. All men, after the choosing of the evil, choose the good. This one, before evil things came forth, chose the good. And this is that he is sinless, that he did not know sin, because even not according to childhood age he sinned, which things are not very difficult, yet they are presented as preceding virtue. This might also be said concerning every saint, through this same thing becoming so in life. He became...

“Behold the man, sent from God, his name John.” “And he shall be filled with the Holy Spirit even from the womb of his mother.” (Luke 1:13-15). Each of these is able to say these words to that: “Upon you I have called from the womb,” that is, “From the womb of my mother, my God you are.” But if concerning Samuel it is said: “And Samuel before knowing God” (1 Sam 3:7), it seems to contend with the things previously said. Therefore let us see more wisely how the word is the will of God.

Job says: “And even if I have eaten my morsel alone and have not shared with the orphan, except as a father guided them from the womb of my mother” (Job 29:15); for how was he able to provide for and care for orphans from the womb of a mother? Thus, therefore, I take it: a praiseworthy practice is a continuous progression; then the practice takes its beginning when the word is fulfilled. I am able, therefore, to say this: he says that I have done good things not after the evil things, but the word having been fulfilled in me, it began from the praiseworthy things; so that we may leave those things entirely, having been brought from elsewhere this state which is “pleasing to God.”

Since, therefore, there is another generation besides the one at hand, and that generation is in a certain way a mother, someone is torn from a womb, from this womb; for not by God alone can a man be brought from this womb into light. And from the breasts which are suitable with milk, which they receive, beginning now to be God-fearing, from those breasts they have hope toward God. And often milk signifies something else: “those turned away from milk; hope upon tribulation they received.” Not he, having ceased from milk just now and having been torn from the breasts of the mother, is able to receive hope upon tribulation.

Often the infant is said to be in relation to the perfect man, with the intermediate ages being passed over in silence: “When I was an infant, when I have become a man” (Ps 22:10, 71:17). And he has become a man not by a first and single change, but by many changes. Therefore, bearing the state of an infant and having a weaker disposition, he is given milk. But when he is able to become someone great, then he is torn from the milk and then he is prepared for athletic power, to pursue and achieve “tribulation upon tribulation and hope upon hope.” “For indeed, owing to be teachers because of the time, again you have need of the...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Unity of Essence and Distinction of Persons
english: To be taught, and you have become in need of milk, not of solid food. You see, that the middle parts were passed over, and the extremes were taken. Often indeed such things are said when the middle parts are passed over.

11 From the womb of my mother, my God, you are (Psalm 22:2). As from the womb of a mother, according to the former explanation from the womb of a mother, Job guides orphans; that is to say, from the womb of a mother, that is to say, from when I began to have knowledge, I served no other god, not my own womb, nor mammon. Or if it is the other, that in this way they descended having God, possessing God. But we do not say this about everyone, but about those who are proclaimed in the Scripture that they have never almost existed in sin, such as John and Jeremiah.

'For you are the one who burst me from the womb.' He said 'to burst' and according to the former probable thought that: since the member of Mary in which she gives birth did not have an exit, she gave birth through the cooperation of God. 'My hope is from the breasts of my mother.' I did not begin to hope after completion, but from the breasts of my mother I had hope in you. If it is understood concerning the holy, we say: the upper Jerusalem is the mother of the saints. From the breasts of this one hope is taken by those who hope, from those who have been discipled by them; for often the breast does not signify the member, but the milk itself.

'Upon you I was cast from the womb, from the womb of my mother, my God, you are' (Psalm 22:9). Upon you I was cast; not toward another was I cast, and then after that toward you. This is given, that from when I began to know piety, I perceived you, I served you. And according to the deeper meaning, that in this way I came to have God with me, just as John. The 'yet shall be filled'; for 'yet' is not said concerning that which has not existed at all.

12 Do not depart from me, for tribulation is near (Psalm 22:10). He speaks concerning the passion. And I need your presence. But when these things are said from the person of the one who was anthropized, it is not said privately toward the Father nor toward the Son, but toward God—one divinity of Father and Son—we say. If, therefore, we say that: 'Christ is the head of every man, but the head of Christ'—he did not say 'the Father', but 'God'; for he receives Christ now as High Priest and as King. Therefore, the head is the divinity.

For if 'the Father' has spoken, he excludes the Son; if 'the Son' has spoken, he overlooks the Father; for he has spoken 'God', since there is one divinity of Father and Son, and one God: indeed, God is one, but Father and Son are not one. Abraham and Isaac are one man, but one is the father and the other the son. Therefore, they are not one according to relation, but one according to essence.

For there is no helper. No one else is able to help. It can also be understood thus: 'for there is not'—I did not cast my care upon another helper. And it can also be: 'for there is no helper to me,' since all are against me, there is no one now, as far as human reasoning goes, who helps. Therefore, do not turn away from me. And it is possible also to say: not even an angel is able to help the one so far off. He does not dare to help because you, being greater than all, that is, the divinity, are present with him, and no one else is of such a kind as to help in this matter.

Many bulls have surrounded me, fattened oxen have enclosed me. Consequently, he speaks of the various factions of the Jews: Pharisees, Sadducees, and the others called Jewish Scribes; for these, in thinking greatly of these animals, are compared to them, especially since these animals are also tillers of the earth. And it is possible to call them bulls, and the fattened oxen are those acting as such, for example: 'the peoples labored in vain' (Ps 106:36)—these are the bulls. 'The kings of the earth stood up' (Ps 2:2). But we do not always perceive kings and rulers; for even a single king, being small and no longer having a kingdom, has been overtaken by the remaining Roman authority.

But Paul interpreted who the rulers are: those who became the cause of the Lord being crucified, of whom he says there are many wisdoms. And he says: 'If they had known, they would not have crucified the Lord of glory' (Acts 4:28). If they had known that they were bringing about the destruction of their own [order], they would not have dared to do this. As we previously said prophetically regarding 'he who touches you touches the apple of his eye' (Zech 2:8): they, having laid hold of the Savior, destroyed themselves; and they rushed to kill him, thinking they would end his rule. On the contrary, it turned out for them: they themselves were destroyed. Fattened oxen have enclosed me; they opened upon me...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
